nodes.label: CI Workflow (vet, build, test on push/PR)
CGO + FTS5 Build Requirement
nodes.rationale: Build and tests require CGO_ENABLED=1 with gcc installed and the 'fts5' build tag for SQLite full-text search; CI fails without these env/tag settings.

nodes.label: Linux amd64/arm64 Cross-Compile Matrix
nodes.rationale: CGO cross-compilation requires a matching C toolchain per arch: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc for arm64, plain gcc for amd64.

nodes.label: Updater Version ldflags Injection
nodes.rationale: Version injected at link time via -ldflags '-X scorp-agent/updater.Version=${VERSION}' (tag name or short SHA) so the released binary self-reports its version.

nodes.label: ReAct Autonomous Tool Loop
nodes.rationale: Agent-first design: every message runs through an autonomous ReAct tool loop instead of plain chat completion.

nodes.label: Surgical Diff Editing (replace_file_content)
nodes.rationale: Replaces exact or fuzzy content chunks instead of rewriting whole files, saving 90%+ tokens with sub-second execution.

nodes.label: read_url Tiered Web Engine (<5MB RAM)
nodes.rationale: Tiered extraction: native HTTP stream -> go-shiori/go-readability cleanup -> JohannesKaufmann/html-to-markdown AST conversion -> cloud scraper fallback (Firecrawl/Tavily) only for bot-blocked or JS-heavy pages, keeping RAM under 5MB.

nodes.label: 3-Tier Autonomy & Security Sandbox (readonly/supervised/yolo)
nodes.rationale: User selects risk level: readonly for safe inspection/audit, supervised (prompts before dangerous commands), yolo for full unattended autonomy.

nodes.label: Outbound Secret Redactor
nodes.rationale: Automatically masks API keys, tokens, private keys and env secrets before tool output reaches the LLM or chat logs; implemented in tools/redact.go, reused as Security Layer 5 for MCP tool output.

nodes.label: Real-Time Steering Queue
nodes.rationale: Allows intercepting and redirecting the agent mid-run without killing the session.

nodes.label: SOP Engine (Standard Operating Procedures)
nodes.rationale: Reusable, declarative automation playbooks invoked via 'scorp sop run <name>' or /sop.

nodes.label: Micro HTTP Gateway & Dashboard (port 8080, ~1.5MB RAM)
nodes.rationale: Built-in web UI designed to run in ~1.5MB RAM for phone/PC browser access.

nodes.label: Native MCP Client (stdio + SSE, JSON-RPC 2.0)
nodes.rationale: Hand-rolled Model Context Protocol client (mcp/client.go, mcp/sse.go) that spawns external MCP servers and registers their tools as native functions; deliberately not using mark3labs/mcp-go.

nodes.label: Multi-Session Management
nodes.rationale: Manage, switch, rename and delete conversation sessions via 'scorp -s <name>' or /session.

nodes.label: Android Termux Static ARM64 Build (make termux)
nodes.rationale: Produces a ~16MB single static ARM64 binary (scorp-termux) runnable on Termux without external libc, with Termux:API integration.

nodes.label: Cryptographic SHA-256 Tool Execution Receipts
nodes.rationale: Every tool execution produces a verifiable SHA-256 receipt, viewable via /receipts, for auditability of agent actions.

nodes.label: Scorp vs PicoClaw vs ZeroClaw Architecture Comparison
Scorp Embedded Native Multi-Engine Metasearch
nodes.rationale: Zero-RAM, zero-Docker metasearch (tools/metasearch.go) running Bing + DuckDuckGo + Wikipedia + GitHub in parallel goroutines: consensus ranking for URLs seen in multiple engines, smart dedup, anti-single-point-of-failure (one blocked engine never fails the agent), pluggable hooks (SEARXNG_URL, BRAVE_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY).

nodes.label: ZeroClaw Third-Party Search Stack (Tavily/Brave/Jina/SearXNG)
nodes.rationale: Search strength driven by commercial API dependencies: Tavily multi-key round-robin, Brave Search API, Jina Reader, Exa, plus optional self-hosted SearXNG.

nodes.label: PicoClaw provider:auto Search Fallback
nodes.rationale: 'provider: auto' automatically degrades to DuckDuckGo scraping when third-party API quota is exhausted.

nodes.label: ZeroClaw Defense-in-Depth Sandboxing
nodes.rationale: Workspace Jail, Path Traversal Blocker, Private IP Blocker, Distroless Docker — layered isolation for corporate/multi-tenant environments.

nodes.label: Scorp Local Simhash & Vector RAG (0 external DB)
nodes.rationale: Knowledge retrieval implemented fully locally without an external vector database.

nodes.label: MCP Marketplace Build Plan & Execution Roadmap
Scorp MCP Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Target for Scorp Agent v2.5/v3.0: registry client, Tri-Option install, transpiler and governance built on top of existing MCP infrastructure rather than from scratch (M0-M2 done, M3 partial).

nodes.label: Tri-Option Install Flow (prebuilt / rebuild / upstream)
nodes.rationale: All three installation options converge on the same endpoint — an entry in ~/.scorp/mcp.json — after which existing infrastructure (watchdog, hot-reload, native tool registry) works automatically; the marketplace is a new sourcing layer in front of the existing mcp_manage, not a new system.

nodes.label: mcp_manage Agent Tool (mcp/manage.go)
nodes.rationale: action=add is the terminal mechanism of ALL install paths; still hardcodes $HOME/.scorp/mcp.json — planned migration to config.ConfigFilePathMCP().

nodes.label: MCP Server Watchdog & Crash Recovery (mcp/watchdog.go, RestartServer)
Native Tool Registry (registry/registry.go)
nodes.rationale: Registers MCP server tools to the LLM via native function calling with deferred tools and raw JSON Schema passthrough.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider LLM Gateway (gateway/gateway.go + models.json)
nodes.rationale: Executes transpiler codegen prompts with complex/premium model routing rules and fallback on error, so the codegen is self-hosted with no external CLI dependency.

nodes.label: AI Transpiler (Self-Hosted Codegen)
nodes.rationale: Converts upstream Node/Python MCP servers into idiomatic Go using scorp's own LLM gateway; manual M0 reference ports double as golden test cases because LLM codegen quality varies.

nodes.label: Transpiler Phase 1: Probe
nodes.rationale: Reuses the JSON-RPC client (mcp/client.go) to spawn an ephemeral upstream server, detect runtime (npx/uvx/python3) and capture initialize + tools/list as the contract benchmark.

nodes.label: Transpiler Phase 2: Generate
nodes.rationale: Structured codegen prompt for mark3labs/mcp-go executed via the gateway with complex-model routing, emitting a single decoupled main.go.

nodes.label: Transpiler Phase 3a: Sandbox Build
nodes.rationale: go build in an isolated temp directory with pinned go.sum and controlled module cache to shrink the supply-chain surface without containers.

nodes.label: Transpiler Phase 3b: Contract Verify & Graceful Degradation
nodes.rationale: Boots the built binary, sends mock JSON-RPC, diffs tool schema against the Phase 1 benchmark (target 100% match); failure yields a transparent blocker report and a fallback offer to the upstream runtime.

nodes.label: Security Layer 1: Source-Only Registry
nodes.rationale: Registry repo policy + CI ensuring only source (not binaries) is accepted from contributors.

nodes.label: Security Layer 2: AST & Prompt Injection Scan
nodes.rationale: gosec + govulncheck + prompt-injection linter run in security-audit.yml on every PR (full multi-maintainer collaboration gate).

nodes.label: Security Layer 3: Hermetic CI/CD
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions multi-arch build pipelines for the registry repo (security-audit.yml, release-binaries.yml, drift-livecheck.yml).

nodes.label: Security Layer 4: SHA-256 Artifact Pinning
nodes.rationale: Client-side checksum verification before executing downloaded prebuilt binaries; Cosign signing deferred to M3 because key management is a project of its own — pure SHA-256 suffices for M1/M2.

nodes.label: wahyuzero/scorp-mcp-registry (public registry repo)
nodes.rationale: Must be public before M1 merge; ports live directly in servers/<name>/main.go for MVP (single source of truth, single CI audit place) resolving the blueprint's 5B/5C inconsistency; port_repository field made optional; drift-livecheck updates registry.json drift fields daily.

nodes.label: mcp-fetch Reference Port (web scraping/markdown)
nodes.rationale: Manually written idiomatic Go port (mark3labs/mcp-go, Go 1.24+) serving as golden standard, first marketplace content, and transpiler validation test case.

nodes.label: mcp-sqlite Reference Port (local DB inspection)
nodes.rationale: Manually written idiomatic Go port serving as golden standard and transpiler validation test case.

nodes.label: mcp-filesystem Reference Port (scoped file access)
nodes.rationale: Manually written idiomatic Go port serving as golden standard and transpiler validation test case.

nodes.label: mark3labs/mcp-go SDK
nodes.rationale: Dependency added ONLY for reference ports and transpiler output; the scorp client itself stays hand-rolled.

nodes.label: Incident Report: Runaway CLI Verify Session (2026-09-05)
nodes.rationale: Two scorp --cli processes ran ~15h at ~170% CPU each (~51 core-hours wasted) with no useful work; detected via (deleted) binary in /proc/<pid>/exe, systemd --user adoption, no network/children; killed manually, no data loss.

nodes.label: CLI Verify Deadloop (no timeout)
nodes.rationale: Suspected root cause: CLI verify sessions from the night of Sept 4 entered a deadloop with no mechanism to stop the process when work never completes, so it survived a rebuild (old inode) until manually killed.

nodes.label: Agent Turn Timeout (context.WithTimeout, SCORP_MAX_TURN_TIMEOUT)
nodes.rationale: Agent execution loop (agent/loop.go) wrapped in context.WithTimeout defaulting to 30 minutes (configurable via SCORP_MAX_TURN_TIMEOUT) so a process can never deadloop forever.

nodes.label: Heartbeat / Stall Detection
nodes.rationale: Context deadline on the HTTP client, max 4 retries, and active-skill ticks detect stalled runs.

nodes.label: Session Lock (cli_lock.go kernel advisory file lock)
nodes.rationale: Exclusive process lock rejects a second CLI process accessing the same session with a clear error plus the active PID (directly targeting the verify_all_ok / verify_all_final collision); pkill + advisory lock on rebuild prevent history-file collisions and orphan processes.

nodes.label: complete_task Explicit Tool Contract
nodes.rationale: Removed heuristic regex/grammar state loops in favor of an explicit termination tool contract, making run completion deterministic instead of pattern-guessed.

hyperedges.label: AI Transpiler Pipeline (Probe -> Generate -> Build -> Verify)
